body: This article was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic.
One bill for Photoshop and Premiere. Another for Word, Excel and PowerPoint. If you are tired of paying two subscriptions every month, ArtCraft is worth a look.

Most of the software we use every day comes from two companies: Adobe for design, photos and video, and Microsoft for office work. Both are now rented, not bought. Stop paying and the apps stop working.

ArtCraft is a response to that. It is a free, open-source set of desktop apps built to replace the main Adobe and Microsoft Office programs. It runs on Windows, Mac and Linux, on your own computer rather than in the cloud.

Its creator calls it a "clean-room" reimplementation: the apps do what Adobe's and Microsoft's software does without copying any of their code or assets. Everything is written in Rust, a programming language known for speed and safety.
◆ In place of Adobe
PhotoCraft — for Photoshop. Layers, masks, adjustment layers, text, and real PSD files.
LightCraft — for Lightroom. A photo library and RAW editing on your own machine.
VectorCraft — for Illustrator.
FilmCraft — for Premiere Pro, for video editing.
EffectCraft — for After Effects, for motion graphics and effects.
DesignCraft — for InDesign, for page layout.
PdfCraft — for Acrobat Pro. Read, merge, split and protect PDFs.
◆ In place of Microsoft Office
WordCraft — for Word. Opens, edits and saves real .docx files.
GridCraft — for Excel. Formulas, charts, and real .xlsx files.
DeckCraft — for PowerPoint, working with real .pptx presentations.
The point here is compatibility: you can open a file someone sent from Office and send it back in the same format. Colleagues on Office won't notice the difference in the file type.
Beyond these, there is CADCraft for AutoCAD-style drafting, SoundCraft for recording and mixing audio, and FigCraft for Figma-style interface design.
◆ Is it really free?
The apps cost nothing and need no account. The code is open source under the MIT or Apache 2.0 licences, so anyone can read or change it.
The team plans to make money by selling access to its AI model inside the apps, alongside models from other companies. Everyday use is free; you pay only if you want AI help.
◆ Installing on a Mac
1. The easiest way is the ArtCraft Launcher. It downloads each app from its official GitHub release and checks the file's SHA-256 fingerprint before installing.
2. Or download only the apps you want from getartcraft.com or the official storytold pages on GitHub. On an Apple Silicon Mac (M1, M2, M3 and later), pick the .dmg marked universal or arm64.
3. Drag the app into Applications. If macOS blocks it the first time, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway."
Note: there is an unrelated iPhone app called "AI Art Generator: ArtCraft." It has nothing to do with this project.
◆ The catch
These are early alpha builds. Saving a PSD can change the file, there are no plugins yet, and bugs are expected. The same caution applies to Office files.
So work on copies, never your originals, and don't cancel your Adobe or Office subscription yet. For now, use ArtCraft alongside the tools you already have.
◆ Why it matters

ArtCraft can't beat Photoshop or Excel today. What it shows is that a serious alternative to both companies' subscriptions is possible, one that runs on your own computer and improves in public with each release.
For students, small businesses and hobbyists, that is reason enough to try it. Download it, explore it, and report the bugs you find.
Sources: pasqualepillitteri.it (ArtCraft apps download page), korben.info, smartworld.it, tech-insider.org
